_purpose: Trace/rare-mineral coverage — the CURATED one-off-rules layer (curated 2026-07-12). The 34 trace_pdm minerals (rare earths plus the other plant-derived traces) have no individual Wallach dose; instead they are covered as a group by plant-derived colloidal mineral intake, measured against Wallach's dose of the colloidal-mineral vehicle (1 fl oz per 100 lb/day, WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000089). This file holds ONLY the editorial JUDGMENT — which products count as a trace/rare vehicle, their group, and whether their mg is derivable — never any amount. All amounts stay sourced from the sealed Products pillar (eden/products/products.json) and are joined in by eden/tools/pdm_coverage_derive.py, so nothing here duplicates a pillar number (R1/derive-don't-duplicate). Hand-authored, manifest 'accounted'.

goal_model.wallach_dose_text: 1 fl oz of liquid plant-derived colloidal minerals per 100 lb of body weight per day
goal_model.reference_serving_note: The maintenance goal (mg) = Wallach's 1 fl oz/100 lb dose expressed in mg via the reference product's composition (Plant Derived Minerals(TM) = 600 mg solids per 1 fl oz serving — Youngevity COMPOSITION, read from the pillar, never hand-typed here), scaled to the 154 lb reference adult (targets_derive BODY_WEIGHT_LB) => ~924 mg/day = 100%.

group_factors._flag_B: Group B (red algae / Aquamin / Lithothamnion) counts 1:1 by DEFAULT, but this factor is the tunable knob: red-algae rare-earth content is NOT established by Wallach's mass-spec (Humic Shale) or Youngevity's published PDM composition, so its mg-equivalence to the Majestic-Earth goal is an ASSUMPTION pending a red-algae rare-earth citation or an explicit ruling. Change this one number to discount Group B.

_products_note: mode 'amount' = the vehicle carries a derivable per-serving mg (nutrient row or blend total) that feeds Sigma mg / 924. mode 'present' = a vehicle IS present but its mg is not derivable (a no-amount other-ingredient carrier, or a trace portion buried in an inseparable proprietary blend) => the hollow/blue 'present' dot, contributes presence not math. group A = Majestic-Earth PDM/humic (Wallach + YGY confirmed full rare-earth spectrum); B = red algae/Aquamin (tunable, see _flag_B); C = Vilcabamba trace minerals; D = generic 'Trace Mineral Complex/Blend' (label-confirmed).

vehicle_supplied._doctrine: Essentials for which Wallach names the plant-derived colloidal mineral vehicle as the SUPPLY ROUTE in his own words. Membership requires a sealed claim in which he instructs the reader to obtain the element FROM the vehicle -- NOT mere presence on the humic-shale roster, which also lists calcium, sodium and potassium and so cannot be the test. These essentials KEEP their own Wallach dose and still cover numerically when a declared item meets it; the vehicle is an ADDITIONAL route, never a replacement. Owner-ratified 2026-08-20, reversing the 2026-08-19 dual-status ruling. Adding an entry here is a SOURCE-RULE act: it must cite the supply sentence, not an inference.

tin.note: Two books 16 years apart carry the same instruction -- 'tin from plant derived colloidal minerals' (Let's Play Doctor 1995, LETS-000451; repeated in Dead Doctors Don't Lie 3e 2011, DDDL-000406/465/466) -- and DDDL-000287 records Wallach's own considerable hair regrowth using plant-derived liquid colloidal tin. A sweep of all seven books finds NO food source for tin anywhere, so the vehicle is the only supply route he ever names for it.

germanium.note: ★ ADMITTED BY OWNER RULING (Luneth, 2026-08-21), NOT by the supply-sentence test above. Wallach names germanium on his own humic-shale roster (WAL-CLM-HELLS-000069, 'Essential Minerals Found in a High Quality Humic Shale'), but nowhere writes 'germanium from plant derived colloidal minerals' the way he does for tin. The roster alone is explicitly NOT the test for the other entries, and that rule still stands for them -- it exists because the roster also lists calcium, sodium and potassium, which all have their own routes. Germanium is the deliberate exception: after its three dose claims were deleted it has NO Wallach amount and NO other covering path of any kind -- it was the only tile in the app unreachable by anything. The plant-derived vehicle is the sole route Wallach associates with it at all. UNIQUE TREATMENT: unlike every other entry here, germanium carries NO numeric target, so the vehicle is its ONLY numeric route rather than an additional one, and it keeps coverage_kind 'dietary_with_clinical_lever' so it stays goal-nameable and shows the amino-style 'no maintenance amount stated' disclaimer instead of the 924 mg group meter. Do not generalise this entry to another essential without a fresh ruling.

vehicle_supplied._hero: OPTIONAL PER-ENTRY FLAG, default true. entity_page_derive._vehicle_hero_slugs() lights the plant-derived HERO (illustration + group story + Best-Youngevity sources) for every member of this registry. Set "hero": false to take the coverage route WITHOUT that editorial block -- the essential still covers off a PDM bottle, but its page carries no plant-derived header and no explainer text. Coverage and hero are deliberately separable: membership here is a COVERAGE fact, the hero is an EDITORIAL choice.

vanadium.note: ★ ADMITTED BY OWNER RULING (Luneth, 2026-08-21), NOT by the supply-sentence test above. Vanadium appears on Wallach's own humic-shale roster in the SAME sealed verbatim table germanium cites -- WAL-CLM-HELLS-000069, 'Essential Minerals Found in a High Quality Humic Shale' -- and on Youngevity's PUBLISHED Plant Derived Minerals composition roster (77 minerals, youngevity.com, roster verified against the vendor listing 2026-08-21), which §00.A permits Youngevity to supply because it is product COMPOSITION, never an amount. Wallach nowhere writes 'vanadium from plant derived colloidal minerals' the way he does for tin, so this entry does NOT pass the supply-sentence test, and that test still stands unchanged for every other essential -- the roster also lists calcium, sodium and potassium. DIFFERS FROM GERMANIUM, which is a SOLE-route exception: vanadium keeps its own numeric Wallach target (150 mcg/day, WAL-CLM-EPIGEN-000138) and is ALREADY covered numerically by declared products (Glucogenix 200 mcg, Slender FX Sweet Eze 200 mcg, both above target). The vehicle is therefore an ADDITIONAL route and this follows the TIN model -- state/coverage.ts takes the BETTER of the vehicle verdict and the numeric one, so removing either side is a behaviour change. NO per-element amount is declared for vanadium in the PDM blend; the owner's ruling is that one 600 mg serving covers the maintenance dose, and that ruling -- not a label number and not a Wallach dose -- is what this entry rests on.
